Kabc020217172021
 In The Court Of The Iv Addl. Small Causes
 And Addl. Mact., Bangalore, (Scch-6)
 Present: Smt. Chetana S.F.
 B.A., L.L.B.,

 Acmm, Court of Small Causes,

P.Ganesh
S/o M.Prakash

.. Respondent JUDGMENT This is a petition filed u/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ with interest from respondent on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident. 
2. The petitioner's case in brief:
That on 2672021 at about 11 a.m. when the petitioner was traveling on a two wheeler bearing reg.NO.KA 03ER2158 on Hosur road, near Hosa road junction bus stop, electronic city, at that time, driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA 42F2148 came in negligently and stopped in the centre of the road and conductor P.Ganesh vs Ksrtc on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198602980/
1 of the bus opened the door suddenly without caring for human safety and dashed against the petitioner, as a result of which JUDGMENT petitioner fell down and sustained injuries and took treatment at hospital. It is further stated that petitioner spent more more amount towards hospitalization, medicine etc., The petitioner was working as a carpenter and earning Rs.25,000/p.m. and due to accidental injuries,
he lost his income and suffering from physical and mental stress. Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.50 lakhs from the respondent. 
3. The respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement. In the written statement respondent contended that at Hosa road bus stop the driver of the bus stopped on the extreme left side of the road in order to get in the passengers, at that time, petitioner who himself came on his two wheeler in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life without observing the traffic rules and regulations, he himself knocked to the KSRTC bus door fell down and sustained injuries. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, exorbitant,
unreasonable and speculative in nature. Hence prays to dismiss the claim JUDGMENT petition. 
4. From the above said pleadings three Issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148 on 2672021 at about 11 a.m. near Hosa road junction bus stop, Hosur main road, electronic city, Bengaluru ? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate? From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and in his support P.W.2 is examined. Exs. P1 to P11 documents are marked. The respondent got examined its driver as RW1 and got marked ExR1 to 3.
6. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record. 
7. My answers to the above issues are as JUDGMENT follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following: REASONS 8 . ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 9 documents as ExP1 to 9 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, spot P.Ganesh vs Ksrtc on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198602980/
2 sketch, charge sheet, wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills.
9. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Ganesh S/o Prakash, electronic city police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed ExP6 charge sheet against the driver and conductor of the KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148 for the offenses punishable under Sec's.283, 338 of IPC, holding JUDGMENT that accident in question has been taken place as accused No.1 the driver of the bus has stopped the bus in the middle of the Hosur main road, national highway in a negligent manner and not stopped the bus in the prescribed bus stop and accused No.2 conductor of the bus without looking for the vehicles behind the bus negligently opened the back side door of the bus which hit the petitioner who was coming on the motor cycle. There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive. 
10. No doubt during the course of his cross examination, RW.1 (driver who was driving KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148 at the time of accident) denied the suggestion that due to his rash and negligent driving the accident has been taken place. But there are no materials on record to believe his version. Further though RW1 stated that false complaint has been filed against him, but has not challenged the same. Thus the unchallenged chargesheet clearly establishes negligence on the part of RW.1. His self serving statement cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident JUDGMENT in order to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects. 
11. On Perusal of the cross examination by the learned counsel appearing for respondent goes to show that the factum of accident is not denied by it. Only suggestions were made to the effect that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148, which were out rightly denied. Under such circumstances oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence produced by the petitioner has to be accepted. 
12. Ex.P7 wound certificate and discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 disclose that the petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., fracture of right leg tibia and POP slab applied. The aforementioned documentary evidence is not controverted by the respondent. Hence there is no reason to disbelieve the same. 
13. Even ExP3 spot mahazar and ExP5 sketch clearly shows that the accident had been taken place on the middle JUDGMENT of the road and the spot of accident was not a bus stop. It clearly shows that the bus was stopped even before the bus stop and in the middle of the road and this fact clearly establishes that as the bus has stopped in the middle of the road and even before the bus stop and as the conductor of the bus has opened the bus for alighting of the passengers the accident has been taken place. Even the respondent has not challenged the said document. 
14. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law. Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted. Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been P.Ganesh vs Ksrtc on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198602980/
3 caused due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148.
15. Even otherwise, it is a settled law that in a claim petition, the claimant need not prove the happening of events beyond reasonable doubt and the rule of preponderance of probability would apply in such cases. In the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC JUDGMENT 2819 (Bimla Devi &
others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others), it has been held that in a Road accident, the strict principles of proof as in a Criminal case are not attracted. Relevant portion of the said decision is reproduced as follows:
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular Bus, in a particular manner, may not be possible to be done by the claimants. The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. The standard of Proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied". 
16. The point that merits consideration is that the degree of proof required for proving the negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F 2148. In the present proceedings, is not as vigorous as is laid in proving the guilt of the accused in criminal trial. The intent of the Motor Vehicles Act is benevolent and the JUDGMENT entire purpose of the Legislation is likely to be defeated if in each case the petitioner is asked to prove the involvement and negligence on the part of the driver beyond reasonable doubt. 
17. Therefore by applying the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the decisions cited supra, to the facts of the instant proceedings, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148 on account of his rash & negligent driving. Hence issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative. 
18. ISSUE NO.2 : As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA42F2148. 
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation. 
JUDGMENT 19. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME : So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 38 years. The petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.7, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner is 39 years and the petitioner has not produced any other documents to prove his age. Hence, the same is considered. The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was carpenter and and earning Rs.25,000/p.m.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income. Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income. In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/ p.m, it would meet the ends of justice. 
P.Ganesh vs Ksrtc on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198602980/
4 20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY: As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : i.e., fracture of right leg tibia, POP slab applied (ExP7 wound certificate). Ex.P8discharge summary JUDGMENT discloses that for the aforesaid injuries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for one day at Blossom hospital, Bangalore and took conservative treatment. 
21. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity. Therefore petitioner got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as PW.2 who stated that in his affidavit that petitioner came with alleged history of RTA and sustained injury to right leg tibia spiral oblique fracture and underwent conservative treatment in the form of above knee POP slab in blossom hospital, Bangalore. It is further stated that petitioner came for disability assessment and following points noted i.e., mild swelling of right leg, ankle, thickening of both bones right leg felt, range of movements of right knee and ankle restricted, daily activities cross leg sittings, squatting for using India toilets were found to be difficulty. PW1 assessed the disability for right lower limb at 41% and 13.33% to the wholebody. PW2 produced OPD record and x ray marked at exP10 and 11.
22. PW2 in his cross examination has admitted that JUDGMENT he has not treated the petitioner. 
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner on the higher side. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343. With regard to the disability in RTA cases,
the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another.
23. But looking into nature and gravity of injuries caused to petitioner that too to his fracture of right leg tibia and from the evidence of doctor, such injuries certainly cause functional disability to the petitioner. Admittedly petitioner being a carpenter and admittedly petitioner has sustained injuries to his right leg and petitioner and it will certainly cause functional disability to the extent of at least JUDGMENT 10% cannot be ruledout. Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 10%. As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of above 39 age is '15'. This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/ p.m. Hence a sum of Rs.2,70,000/ (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 15 X 10/100) which is rounded off to Rs.2,70,000/ is awarded under this head. 
24. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and he has taken the treatment as inpatient for one day. The petitioner has stated that he is still suffering from disability and having severe pain in legs and all over his body. Now he is unable to do his activities as before and his family members are depending on him. Hence petitioner is P.Ganesh vs Ksrtc on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198602980/
5 suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him. On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner JUDGMENT being 39 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony. Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/
under this head. 
25. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD: By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 1 day as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months. Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner it is quite natural that he could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months. Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.45,000/ (15,000 X 3 ) under the head loss of income during the laid up period. 
26. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES: As per discharge summary, petitioner was admitted to the Blossom hospital at JUDGMENT 11.05 a.m. and was discharged on the same day as per the request of the petitioner that petitioner wants to take further treatment at CMC, Vellor. Further PW1 in his cross examination stated that he has taken the treatment in Ayurvedic hospital, but has not produced any document to prove the same. 
Admittedly, though petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 1 day, but certainly,
petitioner has sustained right tibia fracture and he was unable to walk and was dependent on others and it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment and the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges,
conveyance, extra nutritious food etc. Hence a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head. 
27. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: 
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life. Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also JUDGMENT suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life. 
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/ is awarded under this head. 
28. MEDICAL EXPENSES. 
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.10 to 23 i.e.,medical bills and ExP24 to 36prescriptions for Rs.6,563/. The respondent has not disputed the said medical bills, except denial suggestion. Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.6,563/ under the head of medical expenses. 
29. The calculation table stands as follows :
P.Ganesh vs Ksrtc on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198602980/
6 1 Attendant charges, extra : 20,00000 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 50,00000 3 Loss of income during laid : 45,00000 up period JUDGMENT 4 Loss of future income due : 2,70,00000 to disability 5 Loss of future amenities & : 25,00000 happiness 6 Medical expenses : 6,56300 Total Rs.4,16,56300 The said total amount of Rs.4,16,563/ is rounded off to Rs.4,16,600/. Hence petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.4,16,600/.
30. INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice. 
31. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident. Therefore, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount from the date of this order. Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'. 
JUDGMENT 32. ISSUE NO.3: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
: O R D E R : The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,16,600/ with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit. 
The respondent is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order. 
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification and verification. However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time. 
JUDGMENT Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/. Draw award accordingly. 
(Dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open court on this 16th day of February 2024). 
(Chetana S.F.) IV Addl., Small Cause Judge & ACMM, Court of Small Causes,
BENGALURU.
